Hi Monica,

Thanks for the quick chat last week — we're heads-down on product but want to get renewal terms set so our finance team can cut the PO. A couple of asks from my side before we loop procurement: 

- We want a 12-month renewal but need a short-term consumption buffer for the next 3 months to support an expected spike in inference usage.
- Can Redwood provide a price hold for 12 months versus the public list if we keep the same committed baseline?
- We have some unused committed credits from Q2. Instead of forfeiting them, can those be converted to overage/rollover credits at a 1:1 ratio for the next 6 months?

If possible, can you put together a single-page proposal we can share with our procurement? If it's easier, a follow-up call early this week works as well.

Thanks —

Hi Olivia — really appreciate the clear asks. I put a draft offer together and attached the one-pager (renewal-proposal-v3.pdf) for procurement. High level summary: 

- Term: 12 months, effective Aug 1 — Aug 1 start date is flexible if you need time to sign.
- Price hold: we can lock current list-equivalent unit pricing for 12 months if AtlasAI maintains a minimum committed baseline (same as current).
- Consumption buffer: 3-month burst pool (non-expiring for the first 3 months of the term) — up to 15% above baseline for bursts.
- Credit conversion: we can convert up to 25% of unused committed credits from Q2 into overage credits at a 1:1 ratio that can be consumed in the first 6 months of the new term.
- Concession: I'm able to offer a 10% discount on incremental committed units above baseline for the first 6 months if you increase the committed baseline by >=10%.

Next steps I'd recommend: (1) you share the PDF with procurement, (2) we set up a 20-min call to confirm the PO fields, and (3) we provision a draft DocuSign when procurement is ready. I cc'd Marcus (sales leadership) and Hannah (billing) for visibility.

I'll also attach a short usage breakdown from our side so you can see where the burst buffer helps. Happy to tighten language based on procurement feedback.

Best,

- Marcus: can we approve a one-time concession of 10% discount on incremental committed units (first 6 months) if AtlasAI ups baseline by >=10%? This is intended to convert them to a higher commit and reduce their unit cost in ramp months.
- Marcus: also want sign-off to convert up to 25% of Q2 unused credits to overage credits 1:1 for 6 months.
- Hannah: if Marcus signs off, can you prepare a draft invoice and a PO-friendly breakdown that lists the burst pool as a non-billable buffer for the first 3 months? Procurement tends to need that spelled out.

I'm recommending we hold the price for 12 months to avoid back-and-forth later — the business benefit is lower churn risk and a modest upsell. If Marcus prefers a different concession (credits vs deeper discount) let me know.
